hypothesis: Keep the baseline 32-thread table build but reduce PC literal streams per group from 32 to 16. More independent groups for heavily reused Huffman tables may improve scheduling and divergent-tail load balance at large windows, despite increasing regeneration work.
mechanism: Introduce kzstdgpu_StreamsPerGroup_DecompressLiterals, equal to 16 on PC and the existing threadgroup size on consoles. Use it for host prefix/group-count sizing, scalar decoder group offsets and tail bounds, and CPU-emulation group counts. Keep numthreads, table construction, work-item thread stride, Huffman math, and scalar DWORD output unchanged.

expected.performanceClaim: None. This is an unbuilt and unmeasured scheduling hypothesis, not an occupancy or ISA conclusion.
expected.possibleBenefit: For N>16 streams sharing one table, ceil(N/16) independently schedulable groups replace ceil(N/32). A group's active decode set is capped at 16 streams, potentially reducing retention by a small number of long streams.
expected.counterCost: The same change can nearly double group-local table regenerations for heavily reused tables. PR156's 16-stream AMD density used a separately initialized persistent table, so matching density does not reproduce its construction cost.
expected.metric: Unchanged exact CI geometric mean of GB/s at rungs 64,128,192,256,384,512,768,1024; five sweeps per rung using the unchanged perf_manifest corpus and pooling.
expected.requestedEvaluation: Fast funnel: one full unchanged eight-rung CI ladder for this candidate, bracketed by fresh baseline controls. Screen only provisionally; reserve ABBA x3 and conclusive gates for promising finalists.

wiredSurfaces: Host zstdgpu_SubmitStage2 passes the shared streams-per-group constant to ComputePrefixSum.
Unchanged Shaders\ZstdGpuComputePrefixSum.hlsl:59-69 computes ceil(N/streamsPerGroup), inclusive per-table group ends, and total DecompressLiteralsGroups.
Unchanged Shaders\ZstdGpuUpdateDispatchArgs.hlsl:100 feeds the total group count to the existing DecompressLiterals slot.

Unchanged Shaders\ZstdGpuInitHuffmanTableAndDecompressLiterals.hlsl:35,42-45 launches 32 PC threads, preserves the uniform out-of-range guard, and passes tgSize=32 for construction and work distribution.
The scalar decoder multiplies local group index by the shared stream stride and limits its remainder to that stride, while the work-item thread stride stays tgSize.
Both CPU paths call zstdgpu_HufLitStreamCountToGroupCount: GPU-readback replay at main.cpp:576 and standalone CPU emulation at main.cpp:1003. The helper now uses the same shared stream stride.

CPU fused calls retain tgSize=1. The C++ FOR_WORK_ITEMS macro enumerates all items sequentially, so it now decodes every stream in the shared 16-stream group rather than requiring one stream per group.
unchanged: Table generation and expansion algorithm; all 32 PC threads participate before decoding.
Huffman Get/Consume protocol and scalar DWORD head/interior/tail operations.
LDS layout, global resources, bindings, descriptors, SRT declarations, build files, and benchmark files.
Console GPU launch and stream geometry; Xbox One remains 64/64 and Scarlett remains 32/32.
scope.cacheIsolation: The baseline fused entry calls only zstdgpu_DecompressHuffmanCompressedLiterals. StoreLdsCache has a definition but no call site in this worktree, confirmed by source search. e2 is not integrated. Any future pairing must pass the new streams-per-group constant to the cache helper instead of assuming streamsPerGroup=tgSize and independently recheck its active-lane and cache invariants.
scope.portability: All-PC experiment, not AMD-only. The shared fused shader has no added vendor-specific routing or compiled variant. No cross-GPU performance benefit is claimed.

scratchInvariant: The only new state is a compile-time constant. No resource declaration, allocation, capacity, descriptor, binding, or LDS layout changes. Tables remain ephemeral in the same 6456-byte LDS allocation per group, with no persistent or equivalent global table buffer. Per-table prefix arrays retain their old capacity and dispatch storage retains fixed slots. The full 1076-byte global scratch reduction per compressed block is therefore preserved.

correctnessArgument.validation: Source inspection and reasoned bounds/mapping invariants only. git diff --check was clean. No compilation, builds, tests, measurement, remote access, package operations, or delegation.
correctnessArgument.groupPartition: Let S=16 on PC. A table with N streams owns G=ceil(N/S) groups. Group j owns offsets S*j through min(S*j+S-1,N-1). Each offset s has unique owner j=floor(s/S), local index s mod S. Since j<G implies S*j<N for a nonempty table, the remainder subtraction cannot underflow.
correctnessArgument.gpuLaneBounds: All 32 threads finish the existing table build and group barriers. During decoding, the loop starts at threadId and has bound remain<=16 with increment tgSize=32. Thus only threads 0..remain-1 access streams, once each; threads 16..31 perform no decode work. No group barrier is introduced in the divergent decode phase.
correctnessArgument.oneAndFourStreams: N=1 or N=4 still produces one group and respectively one or four decoding owners. Table construction still uses the baseline 32 PC threads.
correctnessArgument.multipleAndPartialGroups: N=16 is one full group; N=17 is a full group and a one-stream tail; N=32 is two full groups; N=33 is two full groups and a one-stream tail. The same quotient/remainder argument covers all N with no duplicate or missing output.
correctnessArgument.treeless: Full-tree stream boundaries and HufWIdToHufLitId are unchanged. Streams from following treeless blocks remain in their original inherited-table range up to the next full-tree start. Only its partition into groups changes.
correctnessArgument.emptySlots: Unused table slots continue contributing zero groups. Existing prefix lookup skips zero-length intervals; a zero total produces no real decode groups. The entrypoint's group-uniform total-count guard stays before table barriers.
correctnessArgument.cpu: The host and both CPU prefix callers share S. C++ FOR_WORK_ITEMS ignores GPU thread parameters and iterates local indices 0..remain-1 sequentially; the CPU still builds each table with tgSize=1, then processes every stream assigned to the group. This maintains the same group boundaries as the GPU without changing decoded values.
correctnessArgument.dispatchCapacity: zstdgpu_EmitDispatch retains its existing one/two-command representation and computes dimensions from the new total. For B blocks whose streams share a table, N<=4*B and ceil(N/16)<=B; summing means the worst-case total group count remains bounded by compressed-block count, as with the baseline's one-table-per-block case. Prefix and indirect-buffer allocation bounds are unchanged.
correctnessArgument.decodeAndOutput: The source edit stops at stream selection. Each stream retains its original input/output segments, one decoding owner, Huffman consumption order, and aligned DWORD/byte stores. Table contents and their final synchronization are unchanged.

risks: Extra table regenerations and dispatch work may dominate any reduction in divergent-tail retention.
With 32 hardware threads but at most 16 decoding streams, full decode groups use at most half the threadgroup. More groups do not guarantee more resident groups or useful occupancy.
A fixed 6456-byte LDS allocation per group can constrain concurrent groups, so reducing stream density can lower useful work per resident group.
Tables with only one or four streams have unchanged group counts and no additional scheduling opportunity.
NVIDIA, Intel, and other AMD hardware may regress; successful RX 6900 XT measurement would not establish portability.
CPU emulation now groups streams like the GPU; the evaluator must exercise both CPU validation paths in addition to GPU correctness.
Future e2 pairing must not retain its streamsPerGroup=tgSize assumption.
